quote: setMessage(`Orders could not be loaded. ${err.message}`, true);
title: A failed reload leaves the previous results on screen under the new filter, with the refund button still enabled
evidence: Driven: loaded all orders, ticked one, switched Status to 'paid' with the API answering 500. The message showed the error, but the table kept the 10 old rows (mixed statuses), the selection survived, and the button read 'Refund 1 order' and was enabled. The catch neither clears state.orders and state.selected nor flags the table as stale.
failing_case: Search for 'smith' fails with 500. The table still lists the previous search's customers beside a search box that says 'smith'. The user takes them for Smith's orders, and a selection made earlier can still be refunded.
remediation: In the catch, clear state.orders and state.selected and call renderStats/renderTable/renderRefundButton so the table is empty, or mark it stale and disable refunds until a load succeeds. Add a Retry button to the error message.

title: Refund eligibility is not checked in the client: refunded, pending and unknown orders can be selected and sent for refund
evidence: Driven: an order with status 'refunded' got a checkbox, the button read 'Refund 1 order', the confirm said 'Refund 1 order totalling $11.00? This sends money back to the customers.', and POST /api/v1/refunds was sent with {"ids":["1"]}. renderRow never disables the checkbox by status, and refundSelected filters nothing. README names what the server must check (user may refund, CSRF, idempotency) but not that the order is refundable.
failing_case: A user ticks an already-refunded order, or a pending one that was never charged, and confirms. A fresh Idempotency-Key is created per click, so the server's idempotency does not catch it. If the server does not also reject the status, money goes out twice or for an unpaid order.

requirement.why: A refund control that accepts refunded or pending orders is implausible for a refund tool; the repo states no eligibility rule.

remediation: Put an isRefundable(order) rule in domain.js (status === 'paid'), disable the checkbox for other statuses, filter picked by it, and state in the README that the server must enforce the same rule.

title: normaliseOrder turns a missing, empty or boolean total into a valid number, so incomplete records are shown and refundable
evidence: Driven in Chromium with a mocked /api/v1/orders. Records with total null, "" and true were kept by normaliseOrder as 0, 0 and 1; only "abc" was dropped. The comment on line 7 says a record with no numeric total returns null. Number(null) is 0, Number("") is 0, Number(true) is 1, and all pass Number.isFinite.
failing_case: The server sends {"id":"x1","total":null,"status":"paid"}. The row shows $0.00, it counts in Orders and drags down Average per order, it can be ticked and refunded, and the 'could not be shown' notice reports nothing for it. In the run, 4 bad records yielded 'skipped: 1'.
remediation: Accept only typeof raw.total === 'number' (or a non-empty numeric string) before converting, so null, '', booleans and arrays are skipped and counted in 'skipped'. Cover it with a unit test for domain.js.

title: Every click makes a new idempotency key, so retrying a refund whose response was lost can refund twice
evidence: Traced. refundSelected calls newIdempotencyKey() on each run. On a network failure the catch keeps state.selected and re-enables the button (finally). api.js line 32 says the key lets the server ignore a repeat for the same attempt, but a user retry is a new attempt with a new key. Only a text warning ('Reload and check the order statuses') stands in the way, and the page has no reload control apart from changing a filter.
failing_case: The server processes POST /refunds but the response is dropped (timeout, wifi switch). The UI says 'The refund was not confirmed'. The selection is intact; the user clicks Refund again and confirms. A new key is sent and the same orders are refunded a second time.
remediation: Keep the key with the pending attempt (same ids, same key) until the server answers definitively, and reuse it on retry. After an unconfirmed failure, call load() so statuses are shown before another attempt.

title: Keyboard focus drops to the page body when Next or Previous disables itself, and the new page is not announced
evidence: Driven: focused #next and pressed Enter twice on a 3-page set. document.activeElement became BODY at 'Page 3 of 3'. The page counter (#page) is a plain span with no live region, so a screen reader hears nothing for the change. WCAG 2.4.3 and 4.1.3.
failing_case: A keyboard user pages forward to the last page. Focus is lost, and the next Tab starts from the top of the document.
remediation: Make #page a role=status/aria-live=polite element, and move focus to #prev or the table caption when the focused pager button becomes disabled; or use aria-disabled instead of disabled.

title: On wide screens the page heading sits 24px left of the content column
evidence: Driven at 1360 px: h1 left edge 130 px, .stats left edge 154 px. main has max-width 1100px with box-sizing border-box and 24px padding, so its content is 1052px wide. The h1 is allowed 1100px of content width inside the header's own padding.
failing_case: At 1360 px wide the 'Orders' heading and the stats cards start at different x positions.
remediation: Give the h1 the same max-width and horizontal padding as main (for example max-width: 1052px) or put both in one shared container class.
